content: Do not dispose of this medication by flushing it down the toilet or pouring it into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. When the product is expired or no longer needed, ensure it is discarded properly according to local regulations or as directed by your healthcare provider or pharmacist. This information was last updated in August 2024. It is important to note that the information provided here is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. The medication, commonly known under the brand name Fuzeon, is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, which allows your immune system to function more effectively. However, enfuvirtide is not a cure for HIV infection. To minimize the risk of transmitting HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Additionally, use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Avoid sharing personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may have come into contact with blood or other bodily fluids. Before using enfuvirtide, read the Patient Information Leaflet and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist. If you have any questions, consult your healthcare professional for guidance on how to prepare and use this medication. Enfuvirtide is administered as an injection under the skin, typically twice daily, as directed by your doctor. The injection should be given in the upper arm, thigh, or abdomen. Avoid injecting into the buttocks or near the elbow, knee, or groin. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. If either is present, do not use the liquid. Clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol before administering each dose. Rotate injection sites to reduce the risk of skin injury. Do not inject into or near bumps from previous injections, moles, scars, bruises, tattoos, burn areas, or the belly button. To minimize bruising, avoid rubbing the injection site after administration. It is crucial to continue using this medication, along with other anti-HIV medications, exactly as prescribed by your doctor. For optimal effectiveness, administer the medication at evenly spaced intervals. Common side effects may include pain, redness, itching, bruising, hardened skin, or bumps at the injection site. These reactions are typical and may last up to seven days. A runny nose may also occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to combat pre-existing infections, potentially causing symptoms of those diseases to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before using enfuvirtide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. HIV treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting the infection to your baby, and enfuvirtide may be part of that treatment. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (such as liver function tests) should be conducted regularly. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly for a new dosing schedule. Before mixing, store the dry powder and mixing solution at room temperature. Once mixed, store the medication in the refrigerator and use it within 24 hours. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
